name: DimensionalDashboardContainer
material_impl: Delegates surface to shared GlassContainer (layout/GlassContainer) per layer; no bespoke blur. Layer opacity computed inline (1 - |z|/(2*depth)). Injects a runtime <style> tag with fixed class names.
motion: Custom rAF auto-rotate via setState every frame (re-renders the whole tree at 60fps); mouse-tilt via state; window scroll listener for parallax. useReducedMotion gates rAF, tilt, parallax and a CSS @media fallback; this is properly wired.
a11y: Layers become role=button + tabIndex + Enter/Space only when onLayerClick is set; focus-visible outline provided. Layers are position:absolute stacked 100% boxes so all but the top layer are unreachable by pointer; screen readers read every layer in DOM order with no grouping/labels.
api: forwardRef to outer div, but does NOT spread rest props (no aria-*, data-*, id passthrough). className concatenated with string template (no cn). layers: ReactNode[] keyed by index. No controlled rotation.
ssr: 'use client'; window only inside effects. Inline <style> duplicated per instance.
fake_complexity: Moderate: 'Z-space positioning' is CSS translateZ on absolute layers; parallax translateZ(scrollY*-0.2) grows unbounded with page scroll and pushes content behind the perspective plane on long pages.
justification: A thin translateZ/tilt wrapper that re-renders on every animation frame and every mouse move, with unbounded scroll-driven translateZ and stacked absolute layers that are not usable as a dashboard container. Reduced-motion handling is one of the better ones in this shard, but the concept is duplicated by DimensionalGlass, GlassDepthLayer, GlassParallaxLayers and Glass3DEngine. Fold the tilt/depth behaviour into one depth primitive driven by CSS variables/motion values instead of React state.
evidence: src/components/dashboard/DimensionalDashboardContainer.tsx:75-80 setRotation inside rAF loop (60fps React renders)

name: GlassActivityFeed
material_impl: Outer GlassCard (shared). Rows use bespoke .glass-activity-neutral-row with hard-coded rgba gradient, rgba border, box-shadow and backdrop-filter: blur(16px) saturate(1.4) brightness(1.08) contrast(1.04) all !important, so every row is its own backdrop-filter layer (72 glass elements in certification DOM). dashboardNeutral.css forces color with !important on p/span/h* and every svg, overriding tokens and status semantics.
motion: Grouped path uses CSS animate-slide-in-up with inline animationDelay regardless of reduced motion; ungrouped path uses shared Motion primitive (MotionFramer honours reduced motion). useReducedMotion is imported but never used. Tailwind arbitrary class built at runtime (duration-[${ANIMATION.DURATION.fast}ms]) cannot be generated by JIT.
a11y: Rows are clickable <div> with onClick, cursor-pointer, no role/tabIndex/key handler, so not keyboard operable. Filter <select> has aria-label. Feed is not a list (no ul/li or role=feed). All 7 activity types return the identical icon colour/bg/border, so error vs success is conveyed by icon shape only.
api: React.FC (no forwardRef). className/style passed. Rest-spread of unknown props onto GlassCard. maxItems/visibleCount state initialised once and not resynced. compact and contained are two booleans for the same mode.
ssr: 'use client'. formatTimestamp uses new Date() during render ('Just now'/'5m ago') and toLocaleDateString without locale, a hydration-mismatch risk.
fake_complexity: None claimed; real but buggy. filterBy prop is ignored in the default grouped path (only applied in filteredActivities, which grouped view does not use); visibleCount is applied per date group instead of globally, so the 'Load more' count is wrong.
target: merge with data-display/GlassTimeline as a single list primitive
justification: Dashboards need an activity feed, but this one flattens status semantics (all types styled the same), stacks a backdrop-filter on every row, overrides tokens with !important, has non-keyboard row actions, and has filter/pagination bugs in its default grouped mode. Rebuild it on a semantic list with rows that are a tokenised inner surface (no per-row blur), real status tones, and roving focus. Then share the row anatomy with GlassTimeline.
evidence: src/components/dashboard/GlassActivityFeed.tsx:399-426 grouped path ignores filterBy and slices visibleCount per group
src/components/dashboard/GlassActivityFeed.tsx:25 useReducedMotion imported, unused; :434-443 CSS animation always on
src/components/dashboard/dashboardNeutral.css:10-36 !important colour overrides on all text and svg

name: GlassChartWidget
material_impl: GlassCard variant=elevated (shared). elevation='level3' is silently overridden to level2 by GlassCard.getElevation for variant=elevated. The action menu is a bespoke glass-surface-dark/80 + backdrop-blur-md popover. .glass-chart-widget-neutral-content * { color: ... !important } forces every chart child (including SVG text/series colours via currentColor) to the theme text colour.
motion: Shared Motion preset fadeIn (reduced-motion aware). Spinner and RefreshCw animate-spin are not gated.
a11y: Icon buttons have aria-labels. The actions menu is a hand-rolled dropdown: no aria-expanded/aria-haspopup, no role=menu, no Escape/outside-click close, no focus management. Fullscreen is just 'fixed inset-4 z-50' with no focus trap, no Escape, no scroll lock, and no backdrop.
api: React.FC, no forwardRef. Fullscreen is half-controlled: the fullscreen prop only seeds useState and is never synced. Refresh/Export appear both as quick actions and as hard-coded menu defaults. GlassChartWidgetGrid uses widget.title as key.
ssr: 'use client'; relative time in render via new Date() (hydration risk).
target: templates/dashboard/widgets/ChartWidget + charts ChartContainer -> one GlassWidget/Panel with header actions slot
justification: A reasonable chart-frame idea, but it overlaps with the template ChartWidget, ChartContainer and WidgetGlass. Its menu and fullscreen are not accessible overlays, and the !important colour override breaks the series colours of any chart placed inside. Keep one dashboard panel primitive that uses the library's real Menu/Dialog primitives for actions and fullscreen.

src/components/dashboard/dashboardNeutral.css:56-59 forces colour !important on all chart descendants

name: GlassKPICard
material_impl: GlassCard (shared), with props depth/intensity/border/performanceMode/animation that GlassCard does not declare in its own interface; they are presumably forwarded to OptimizedGlass. Icon chip is bespoke bg-gradient-to-br from-white/10 border-white/20. The hover glow repeats 'glass-gradient-primary' three times plus via-purple, and adds hover:shadow-purple-500/20, giving off-brand purple glows. Variant colours use raw Tailwind palette (text-green-400, red-400, yellow-400, blue-200), not tokens.
motion: Motion fadeIn (reduced-motion aware). Hover scale/rotate-2 on icon and drop-shadow transitions are CSS and not reduced-motion gated. Duration classes are runtime-interpolated arbitrary Tailwind values that will not compile.
a11y: Clickable via GlassCard (role=button + Enter/Space handled in GlassCard). Trend is colour+arrow; trend text has no sr-only direction ('up 12%'). ContrastGuard wraps text. The error variant colours trendUp red, so 'up' is shown red with no explanation.
api: React.FC, no forwardRef, no style prop. Default title 'KPI' on a required prop. `previousValue && ...` hides a legitimate 0. size/variant naming matches the siblings, but this is the third copy of the same card.
fake_complexity: 'premium glow effect' is a hover gradient blur that only works if the arbitrary classes exist.
target: single GlassStatCard (KPI/Metric/Stat merged) built on data-display/GlassMetricChip tokens
justification: This is roughly 80% the same code as GlassMetricCard and GlassStatCard (same size/variant tables, same skeleton, same trend block, same Grid helper), using raw Tailwind palette colours and purple hover glows that do not belong to a neutral glass system. Merge the three into one stat card with slots (trend, sparkline, progress, comparison) and token-driven status tones, then keep GlassKPICard as a deprecated alias.
evidence: src/components/dashboard/GlassKPICard.tsx:111-192 size/variant tables duplicated verbatim in GlassMetricCard.tsx:151-258 and GlassStatCard.tsx:146-251

name: GlassMetricCard
material_impl: Same as GlassKPICard: GlassCard plus a bespoke gradient icon chip, a triple-gradient purple hover glow, hover:shadow-blue-500/20, and raw Tailwind progress colours (bg-green-500 etc.).
motion: Motion fadeIn/slideRight (reduced-motion aware via MotionFramer); CSS hover transforms not gated; arbitrary runtime duration classes.
a11y: The progress bar is a div with no role=progressbar/aria-valuenow. The trend has no text direction. ContrastGuard is missing on the main value (unlike the KPI card). Loading skeleton has no aria-busy.
api: The best of the three: forwardRef, extends HTMLAttributes, adds valueClassName/valueStyle. However the ref is NOT applied in the loading branch, and onClick is typed () => void, overriding the DOM signature.
target: single GlassStatCard (use GlassMetricCard's forwardRef/HTMLAttributes API as the base)
justification: Its API is the strongest of the three stat cards, so it should be the base of the merged component. The progress bar still needs ARIA, the status palette needs tokens, the purple/blue hover glows should go, and the ref must forward in every branch.

name: GlassStatCard
material_impl: GlassCard variant default/elevated (shared). Hover:shadow-emerald-500/20, raw Tailwind palette, and a triple glass-gradient-primary progress fill.
motion: Motion fadeIn/slideRight (reduced-motion aware). No hover transforms on this one.
a11y: Sparkline SVG has no role=img/title/aria-label. Progress bar has no ARIA. additionalStats render without ContrastGuard.
api: React.FC, no forwardRef, no style. Sparkline height is derived by parseInt of a Tailwind class string ('h-8' -> 8*4=32px), while the svg height attribute is set to the raw number (8), so the path is drawn in a 32px coordinate space and clipped/overflowing in an 8px-high svg. Sparkline x uses percent numbers in a viewBox-less svg, so x is 0-100 px, not percent.
fake_complexity: The 'sparkline' is a broken mini-chart (see api).
target: single GlassStatCard (absorb KPI/Metric; replace sparkline with charts primitive)
justification: This is the third copy of the stat-card pattern. Its one differentiator, the sparkline, is geometrically broken: a 32px path coordinate space inside an 8px svg with pixel-not-percent x values. Keep the name for the merged component, but rebuild the sparkline on the charts package with a viewBox and accessible labelling.
evidence: src/components/dashboard/GlassStatCard.tsx:420-423 svg height={'8'} without viewBox; x 0-100 used as px

name: EnhancementShowcase
material_impl: Ad-hoc utility soup: repeated 'glass-gradient-primary glass-gradient-primary glass-gradient-primary' strings, glass-surface-subtle/5 + backdrop-blur-lg panels, and bg-${color}-400 dynamic Tailwind classes that cannot compile. Uses an EnhancementShowcase.module.css for the header and nav.
motion: AnimatePresence section transitions. Under reduced motion animate={} while initial={opacity:0}, so the active section stays invisible at opacity 0. Composes Physics/Morphing/3D/Organic engines, which add their own ungated motion.
a11y: Nav buttons have aria-current. However the content collapses to invisible under reduced motion. The nav is a tab pattern without tablist semantics.
ssr: Reads `window.COMMON_SEQUENCES` directly during render (lines 304 and 542), which throws ReferenceError on the server. Imports framer-motion plus every 'engine' and both intelligence hooks.
fake_complexity: Severe: marketing copy for 'consciousness interface technology', 'Emotional Intelligence', 'Biometric Adaptation', 'WebXR Integration' and 'AI/ML systems'. The status tiles ('Physics Engine: Active', 'AI Intelligence: Learning') are hard-coded literals. useEmotionalIntelligence and useAIPersonalization feed displayed percentages.
justification: This is a non-exported demo page that crashes under SSR (window in render), shows nothing to reduced-motion users, uses uncompilable dynamic classes, and makes unverifiable AI, emotion and biometric claims through hard-coded status labels. It is directly harmful to the premium positioning. Delete it, and let the LiquidGlassShowcase/docs site present only the components that actually ship.
evidence: src/components/demo/EnhancementShowcase.tsx:683-684 initial opacity 0 + animate {} when reduced motion
reports/glassmorphism-storybook-visual-certification.json EnhancementShowcase: 880 visible elements, hasCanvas=true (from nested engines)

name: GlassEcommerceProvider
material_impl: None. It is a context provider plus a wrapper div. data-glass-component is put on Context.Provider, where it is meaningless.
api: The value object is rebuilt on every render without useMemo, so every consumer re-renders on any state change. useEcommerce silently returns a no-op default context instead of throwing, which hides missing-provider bugs. useEcommerce and every type (Product, CartItem...) are NOT exported from the root index, so consumers cannot read the context they provide. Initial products/cart cannot be injected (no props). Tax is hard-coded at 8% and currency at '$'.
fake_complexity: Severe: 'Mock AI recommendation engine' with a 1s setTimeout and Math.random scores and confidence; getAnalytics returns hard-coded totals (1250 views, 7.1% conversion) and random per-product numbers; trackEvent and getPriceAlerts are empty mocks; the mock shipping/payment options use emoji icons.
target: move to examples/ or a separate demo package
justification: A design-system package should not ship a mock commerce backend: hard-coded tax, USD, random 'AI' recommendations, fake analytics, and state-mutating sort bugs, while not even exporting the hook needed to use it. Remove it from the library surface. If a commerce kit is needed, ship presentational, fully-controlled components and leave state to the app.
evidence: src/components/ecommerce/GlassEcommerceProvider.tsx:573,629-650 filtered===products then Array.sort mutates React state in place
src/index.ts:709 only GlassEcommerceProvider exported; useEcommerce/types not exported

name: GlassProductRecommendations
material_impl: Outer Glass primitive (shared). Cards use glass-surface-subtle/border utilities. Reason chips use raw Tailwind palette (bg-blue-500/20 text-blue-200 etc.). The overlay is bg-black bg-opacity-50 (Tailwind v2 syntax). The 'AI' badge uses inline colour #334155 on a dark glass surface, and the fallback artwork uses hard-coded light-slate hex.
motion: CSS hover scale on images and a carousel translateX transition; no reduced-motion gating; no framer.
a11y: The card wrapper is a clickable div with no role or keyboard support. Quick actions sit in an opacity-0 hover overlay that stays focusable and clickable while invisible, and is unreachable visually on touch. Emoji-only buttons (heart, cart) rely on title only. Carousel arrows (arrows as text) have no aria-label and no live region. The star rating has no text alternative.
api: React.FC, no forwardRef, no style. getItemsPerView is a hard-coded 4/8 regardless of viewport, and the carousel grid is glass-grid-cols-4 on mobile. Currency is hard-coded '$'. getReasonColor/getReasonIcon are duplicated in the card and the parent.
fake_complexity: Severe: when products are passed explicitly it fabricates reason ('personalized' for index 0, 'similar' for 1, then 'trending'), score and confidence, and labels them 'Match confidence'. The 'AI Insights' copy claims 'personalized based on your browsing history... Our AI analyzes N factors', where N is just the list length.
target: if commerce is in scope: rebuild as presentational GlassProductCard + LiquidGlassCarouselRail
justification: It invents recommendation reasons and confidence percentages for caller-supplied data and presents them as AI output, which is a trust and legal liability for any adopter. It is also emoji-iconed, not keyboard accessible, and a fixed 4-column carousel on mobile. Remove it. A future commerce kit should be a controlled product card composed with the existing carousel rail.

name: GlassSmartShoppingCart
material_impl: Glass primitive outer (shared). Interior uses border utilities, raw border-blue-400/60 bg-blue-500/15 for the selected shipping option, and an inline #334155 empty-state icon (low contrast on dark glass).
a11y: The close (multiplication sign) and remove buttons rely on title only, with no aria-label. The quantity +/- buttons have no labels and no live region; the quantity shows '...' during a fake delay. The promo input has no label (placeholder only). The 'Remove' promo button has no handler. The radio group has no fieldset/legend.
api: React.FC, no forwardRef, no style. The items prop makes it display-only: quantity/remove/save call the context's no-op updaters, so the controlled mode is broken (UI quantity changes locally, totals do not). showRecommendations is declared and never used. Hard-coded USD, 8% tax, and a $50 free-shipping rule.
fake_complexity: Severe: nothing 'smart'. Fake 300ms 'API delay' on quantity change and a 1s fake promo validation. Valid promo codes SAVE10/WELCOME20/FREESHIP are hard-coded in the shipped library (anyone can apply discounts client-side). It renders the claim 'Secure checkout with 256-bit SSL encryption' regardless of the host app.
target: if commerce is in scope: rebuild as controlled GlassCartSummary + GlassQuantityStepper
justification: It hard-codes discount codes, tax, currency and a security claim into a UI library. Its controlled mode silently does nothing, its icon buttons are unlabeled, and it simulates network latency with setTimeout. None of this is salvageable as a design-system component. Remove it, and if needed provide a controlled cart summary and quantity stepper that hold no business logic.
evidence: src/components/ecommerce/GlassSmartShoppingCart.tsx:428-440 items prop totals vs context updaters (no-op)

name: GlassRichTextEditor
material_impl: OptimizedGlass shell (shared primitive, elevation prop). The toolbar and every tool button carry bespoke inline rgba gradients, borders and box-shadows plus an injected <style> with !important hover rules. These are not tokens and assume a light surface (hover rgba(255,255,255,0.36)).
motion: CSS translateY hover with a prefers-reduced-motion override (wired).
a11y: role=toolbar with aria-label; tool buttons have aria-label; the editable has role=textbox, aria-multiline, and a hard-coded aria-label 'Rich text editor' that cannot be overridden (rest props go to the outer shell, not the textbox). No aria-pressed/active state for B/I/U. No roving tabindex in the toolbar. The link tool uses window.prompt().
api: forwardRef to outer shell. Controlled-only in practice: in uncontrolled use, `!value` stays true, so the placeholder overlays typed content whenever the editor blurs. No sanitisation hook. No name/form integration.
ssr: 'use client'; document.execCommand / prompt only in handlers.
fake_complexity: None, but it is built on deprecated document.execCommand.
target: headless editor (Tiptap/Lexical) adapter wrapped in OptimizedGlass + shared LiquidGlassToolbar
justification: Writing the value prop straight into innerHTML with no sanitisation is a stored-XSS vector, and createLink accepts javascript: URLs from prompt(). It relies on deprecated execCommand, has no active-state feedback, and its placeholder overlaps typed text in uncontrolled mode. The glass shell is fine. Keep the visual wrapper and replace the engine with a maintained headless editor, using the library's LiquidGlassToolbar for the controls.
evidence: src/components/editor/GlassRichTextEditor.tsx:320-324 prompt() URL passed to createLink unvalidated

name: AuroraPro
material_impl: The r3f implementation uses three.js ShaderMaterial waves and points plus bespoke overlay chips (glass-surface-dark). The wrapper fallback is a plain div. Palettes are hard-coded Material-colour hex values; the 'custom' default passes CSS var strings into THREE.Color, which three cannot parse.
motion: useFrame loop, never gated by reduced motion. The overlay chips use initial opacity 0 + animate {} under reduced motion, so they stay invisible. particleDrift adds sin() to the already-mutated x every frame (random walk drift; particles wander off).
a11y: Control buttons are title-only (no aria-label/aria-pressed). The palette buttons do nothing ('Would update colorPalette prop'). The canvas has no aria-hidden.
api: Exported only via the 'aura-glass/three' subpath. No forwardRef/style. The fallback spreads all effect props (intensity, speed, colorPalette...) onto a DOM div, causing React unknown-prop warnings.
ssr: The wrapper lazy-imports the r3f chunk in an effect (good pattern). But the gate assertReact19ForThree checks React.__SECRET_INTERNALS_DO_NOT_USE_OR_YOU_WILL_BE_FIRED for key 'S'. In React 18 (installed 18.2.0) that object has no 'S', and React 19 removed that export altogether. The check can never pass, so the R3F path is dead code: certification shows hasCanvas=false.
fake_complexity: Total: the shipped component always renders an empty div. If the R3F path ever ran, the fragment shader contains the JS line `const prefersReducedMotion = useReducedMotion();` inside the GLSL noise() function and would fail to compile. getPaletteColors calls a hook inside a nested function invoked a variable number of times (Rules of Hooks violation). Geometries and materials are never disposed.
justification: This is a broken R3F demo hidden behind a version gate that can never succeed, so users get an empty div. Even unlocked, the shader would not compile because a React hook call is pasted into GLSL, the hooks usage violates React rules, and it leaks GPU resources. The story text even admits the fallback. Three other aurora components already exist; delete this one and the 'three' subpath entry.

src/components/effects/AuroraPro.r3f.tsx:433-439 hook inside getPaletteColors called in loops
src/components/effects/AuroraPro.tsx:20,44-56 gate + fallback div spreading non-DOM props

src/utils/reactVersion.ts:7-15 checks React.__SECRET_INTERNALS_DO_NOT_USE_OR_YOU_WILL_BE_FIRED for 'S'; React 19 renamed that object to __CLIENT_INTERNALS_DO_NOT_USE_OR_WARN_USERS_THEY_CANNOT_UPGRADE, so the gate returns false on React 18 AND 19: the three R3F effects can never render (re-verified 2026-10-06).

name: Glass3DEngine
material_impl: Bespoke: inline hsla holographic gradients per layer, mixBlendMode multiply/overlay, conic-gradient overlay, CSS blur filters per layer and per SVG circle, and an feTurbulence/feDisplacementMap filter per layer. A comment says 'Use createGlassStyle() instead', but the code does not. No tokens except var(--glass-bg-default).
motion: framer springs for tilt, useScroll parallax, autoDemo infinite loops. shouldAnimate gates autoDemo/holographic, but mouse tilt springs, whileHover, whileTap and scroll translateZ are NOT gated, and the .interaction-pulse CSS animation is infinite and ungated.
a11y: Purely pointer-driven. Click does nothing for keyboard users. Decorative layers are not aria-hidden. Children are the only content.
api: React.FC; Glass3DEngineProps not exported; no forwardRef; no style/rest passthrough; template className. 'gaze'/'proximity' interactions are declared but unimplemented; refractionIndex is unused. Sub-variants (ParallaxGlass, DepthGlass, HolographicGlass, InteractiveGlass3D) are not exported from root.
ssr: 'use client'; useScroll at module-level hook is fine.
fake_complexity: High: 'Immersive 3D Glass Effects Engine' is CSS translateZ plus gradients. 'refraction' is unused. DistortionMesh and DepthOfFieldLayer are components declared inside render, so they get a new identity every render: every mouse move remounts all of them and their SVG filters. Each also has a conditional early return before useMemo (Rules of Hooks). Default config produces 8 meshes x 81 blurred circles plus 8 turbulence filters. SVG filter ids collide across instances.
justification: Component-in-render remounting on every mousemove, around 650 blurred SVG nodes, conditional hooks, colliding filter ids and ungated tilt make this a performance and a11y liability. Its 'engine' claims (refraction, gaze, proximity) are not implemented. Pointer tilt and depth layering already exist elsewhere. Remove it and offer a single cheap useTilt hook and depth primitive.

src/components/effects/Glass3DEngine.tsx:293-316 81 points per mesh; :366-368 per-circle CSS blur

name: GlassMorphingEngine
material_impl: Bespoke: seven stacked .glass-layer divs in glass-morphing.css driven by --gm-* CSS variables (rgba white gradients, conic crystalline, caustic shimmer). Ten framer springs write CSS variables imperatively (a good technique, poor payload). Not built on OptimizedGlass or LiquidGlassMaterial.
motion: Springs plus a CSS caustic-shimmer infinite animation. useReducedMotion is called but its result is never used, and glass-morphing.css has no prefers-reduced-motion block, so the infinite shimmer is always on.
a11y: Decorative layers are not aria-hidden; otherwise transparent wrapper.
api: React.FC; props interface not exported; no forwardRef; className/style supported. enableRealTimeAdaptation defaults to true, and the mocked 'real-time' data is spread AFTER the caller's environmentalContext. Any timeOfDay/weather/season the caller passes is therefore overwritten by the clock and the hard-coded 'sunny'. The default environmentalContext={} is a new object every render, so the effect runs every render. A test-env branch checks process.env.JEST_WORKER_ID in production code.
fake_complexity: Self-declared '@demo ... uses in-component mock data'. fetchEnvironmentalData returns weather 'sunny', 22C, 45% humidity, 75% light, all constants. 'refraction', 'viscosity' and 'temperature' map only to white-gradient alpha.
duplicates: src/components/advanced/GlassEngine.tsx (EnvironmentalGlass/AdaptiveGlass; name collision with this file's EnvironmentalGlass)
justification: It is a self-declared demo that, by default, ignores the context props it advertises, runs an ungated infinite shimmer, and ships Jest-detection branches in production code. The CSS-variable-driven spring pipeline is the only reusable idea, and that belongs in LiquidGlassMaterial as documented tunables, not in an 'environmental engine' with fake weather.

src/components/effects/GlassMorphingEngine.tsx:280 prefersReducedMotion unused; src/components/effects/glass-morphing.css:43-55 infinite animation, no reduced-motion block

name: GlassPhysicsEngine
material_impl: No material; canvas 2D particles with random hsl(180-240) colours, shadowBlur 10 and mixBlendMode screen, plus a radial-gradient pulse overlay.
motion: framer keyframes for bend/melt/vibrate, plus a canvas particle loop. triggerInteraction is gated by shouldAnimate, but mouse tilt (rotateX/rotateY springs) is NOT gated. The animate-pulse overlay is ungated.
a11y: Effects are click-only; there is no keyboard trigger. The tabIndex passthrough exists only so it can be removed. The canvas is not aria-hidden.
api: React.FC; props interface not exported; no forwardRef/style. Six alias components (ShatterGlass, RippleGlass...) are not root-exported.
ssr: 'use client'; window resize in effect only.
fake_complexity: High: the 'Physics simulation' is Euler particles stepped through React setState every frame. The updater mutates particle objects in place (impure, so StrictMode double-invocation doubles the physics). getBoundingClientRect is called per particle per frame (layout thrash). renderParticles draws the stale `particles` closure, one frame behind. physicsConfig is a new object every render, which recreates animate and restarts the rAF effect on every render. The canvas is not DPR-scaled (blurry on retina). viscosity/refractionIndex/density are unused.
target: visual-feedback/RippleButton (press feedback) as the supported interaction effect
justification: A 60fps React-state particle loop with impure updaters, per-particle layout reads and an rAF restart on each render is not shippable, and cyan sparks with screen blending do not read as premium glass. Press-ripple feedback already exists in RippleButton. Remove it, or at most reimplement a single GPU-cheap press highlight inside the material primitive.
evidence: src/components/effects/GlassPhysicsEngine.tsx:113 physicsConfig new object each render -> :155-192 -> :250-286 rAF restart
src/components/effects/GlassPhysicsEngine.tsx:157-187 mutates particles in place inside setState updater

name: GlassShatterEffects
material_impl: r3f ShaderMaterial shards (fresnel tint). Fallback is a plain div. Controls use glass-surface-subtle utilities.
motion: Custom Date.now() lerp animations in useFrame; no reduced-motion gating of shatter/explosion; overlays invisible under reduced motion (animate {}).
a11y: Trigger is a native addEventListener click on a div, so it is not keyboard operable. The control button is title-only. On shatter, children fade to opacity 0 but stay in the a11y tree.
api: Exported only via the 'aura-glass/three' subpath. No forwardRef. The fallback spreads non-DOM props (duration, intensity, onShatter...) onto a div.
ssr: Lazy import behind assertReact19ForThree, which never returns true (see AuroraPro), so the R3F path never loads: certification hasCanvas=false.
fake_complexity: Total and doubly broken: (1) Shards are generated in a mount effect guarded by `if (!canvasRef.current) return`, but the Canvas only mounts after isShattered, so the shard list is always empty. (2) createExplosionAnimation calls useReducedMotion() inside a plain function invoked from a click handler, which throws 'Invalid hook call' on the first shatter. (3) Reform never resets isShattered (`if (!isShattered) setIsShattered(false)`), and the autoReform setTimeout captures a stale triggerReform, so content stays at opacity 0 permanently.
justification: Even if the dead version gate were fixed, the effect would crash on the first click (hook call outside render), render zero shards, and leave the wrapped content permanently invisible. Math.random in the reset breaks the seed contract. createRainMaterial/rainFall are unused.
